note: Computed prospects from the 2022 LiDAR (1 m DEM, 2 m analysis). Screening only: every site needs checking on the ground, and dams, walls and pads need engineering and council approval.

items.label: P1 pond · ~0.2 ML
items.note: 3 m wall about 16 m long holds about 0.2 ML (222 m³) over 172 m². Wall earthworks roughly 284 m³. 3.6 ha drains to it. Small catchment: the easiest kind of in-gully pond; still needs a spillway. High on the lot: a gravity source for the benches below.

items.label: B1 building pad · 125 m
items.note: Level 16 × 16 m pad at about 125 m needs roughly 92 m³ of cut and fill (up to 2.2 m deep). About 9.3 h of winter sun (terrain only), north-east-facing. On a spur: above the cold-air drainage, good airflow, but more exposed to wind and to fire running upslope; keep a cleared, low-fuel zone around it.

items.label: T1 header tank · 148 m
items.note: Highest workable spot on the lot. A tank here gives about 2.3 bar at the 125 m pad, about 6 bar at the 87 m benches and about 9 bar at the 55 m gully floor, so use pressure-reducing valves below about 100 m. Fill by pump from the ponds, or by roof water from a shed nearby.

items.label: F1 gully flat · 692 m²
items.note: One of only three areas under 18% slope, at about 60 m on the northern gully floor. Easiest ground for a dug off-creek pond, nursery, or frost-hardy beds; cold air pools here on still nights and it is close to flood flows.
